evidence.positive:
Drove the real rule-engine path on the running app (localhost:57959, demo-demo, patient-2 / case 10001, launched via POST /api/app-launch). Staged an active insulin infusion (POST /api/admin/infusion/patient/patient-2/10001, m-insulin-regular, START 1.0 units/hr 3h ago), an eGFR observation with the unreadable Mayo-style value ">90" (POST /api/admin/observations/... type EGFR), then two glucose observations (300 then 200 mg/dL) which fire EventCategory GLUCOSE_UPDATED. The app log shows 'Rule evaluated: a-adjust-insulin-infusion-rate -> true null' and a row landed in demo-demo.rule_fired_results with prompt title "Change Insulin Infusion Rate to 0.5 Units/hr", description "Blood glucose = 200 mg/dL. Recommend changing the insulin infusion rate to 0.5 Units/hr." and EXPANDED_CALCULATION = 'Updated ISC = 0.005 - (0.005 × 0.25) = 0.0038, because of a glucose drop ≥ 75mg/dL.
ISC has been adjusted for Type 1 Diabetes' — alert delivered, eGFR clause correctly absent, zero NullPointerExceptions in the log.
evidence.negative:
Re-ran the same glucose event against five eGFR states, reading EXPANDED_CALCULATION straight out of rule_fired_results each time. Unreadable values ">90", "<15", "" (empty) and no eGFR row at all all produced '...
ISC has been adjusted for Type 1 Diabetes' with no eGFR clause, and the alert fired every time (fired-row count went 1→2→3→4→5→6). Numeric eGFR 90 (readable, >= 45) likewise produced no eGFR clause. So the eGFR adjustment is not asserted for any value the app cannot read as a number, including "<15" whose bound is below 45 — matching the ticket's stated intent (reading the inequality bound is OR-2744).

automation.assessment: The fix already ships good unit coverage in AdjustInsulinInfusionRateRuleTest: testExpandedCalculationOmitsEGFRWhenValueIsNotNumeric is parameterized over null, ">90", "<15", ">" and "SEE" and asserts both isNeedsAction() and the exact calculation string, and testExpandedCalculationCitesEGFRWithoutDiabetesTypeOne locks in the numeric-low case. Nothing there needs duplicating. The gap is that those tests mock ObservationService, so they cannot catch what actually broke in production — the rule aborting inside the engine and the alert never being persisted. That end-to-end shape is what I exercised by hand and is worth locking in, plus the one input combination the parameterized test does not reach (unreadable eGFR on a patient without Type 1 diabetes, where the calculation should carry no adjustment clause at all).
proposed_tests: qa-suite (supplemental, insulin/glucose family): stage an insulin infusion + eGFR ">90" + two glucose observations via the admin API, then assert the insulin-rate alert is returned and its Show Calculation text contains no "eGFR" — the engine-level regression the mocked unit tests cannot see.

Unit (AdjustInsulinInfusionRateRuleTest): unreadable eGFR on a patient WITHOUT ConditionTag.DIABETES_TYPE_1 — assert the alert still fires and the calculation carries no adjustment clause at all; the existing parameterized test only covers the Type 1 variant.
Unit (AdjustInsulinInfusionRateRuleTest): eGFR of "90" (numeric, >= 45) — assert no eGFR clause, so the suppression is pinned to the threshold and not just to unreadability.

jira_comment:
**Verdict: deploy-ready.** Validated against the merged `main` build in a disposable local instance (demo-demo, patient-2 / case 10001) by driving the real GLUCOSE_UPDATED path: active insulin infusion, an eGFR observation, then glucose readings through the admin API.

- **Positive** — with the Mayo-style unreadable eGFR `">90"`, the rule evaluates cleanly and the alert lands: *"Change Insulin Infusion Rate to 0.5 Units/hr"*, with the Show Calculation reading *"ISC has been adjusted for Type 1 Diabetes"* and no eGFR clause. No NullPointerException anywhere in the log.
- **Negative** — repeated for `"<15"`, an empty value, no eGFR row at all, and numeric `90`. None of them produce an eGFR clause, and the alert fires every time. Note `"<15"` is deliberately dropped despite its bound being under 45 — reading the inequality is OR-2744.
- **Red check** — I compiled the pre-fix version of `AdjustInsulinInfusionRateRule` and swapped it into the running container. The same scenario immediately went red: no alert row at all, and `NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "java.lang.Float.floatValue()" ... getNumericObservationValue() is null` in the log — the exact crash from this ticket. I restored the shipped class (checksum verified), restarted, and confirmed the alert fires again. I also flipped the eGFR to a real `30` and watched the clause reappear, so the "clause is absent" assertion can genuinely fail.

The unit tests that shipped with the fix already cover the non-numeric inputs well. For automation I'd add an end-to-end qa-suite case (the mocked unit tests can't see the rule aborting inside the engine) plus two small unit cases: unreadable eGFR without Type 1 diabetes, and a numeric eGFR of 90.
